title: The module-valued constant sheaf functor on a connected scheme is fully faithful
statement: Let X be a scheme with nonempty connected underlying topological space [def-weil-connected-scheme], and let B be any commutative ring. On its small etale site, the constant-sheaf functor [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] from B-modules to sheaves of B-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is fully faithful: every morphism between two constant module sheaves comes from a unique B-linear map of the coefficient modules. In the Lean universe convention, X : Scheme.{u} and B : Type (u+1). No finiteness, field, or nontriviality assumption on B is required.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps, and the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction; exact existing Lean proof: WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ModulePointFunctions.lean, fullyFaithfulModuleConstantSheaf, lines 210-220

proof.text: The module-valued constant sheaf has the same locally constant section description as its underlying additive group. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected], for every B-module M the canonical constant-section map M -> Gamma(X,underline M) is bijective. Its restriction maps and the canonical map respect B-scalar multiplication, so this is an isomorphism of B-modules. Equivalently, the source proof shows injectivity by evaluation in the module sheaf of functions on points, and surjectivity because sheafification is locally constant and a locally constant function on the connected nonempty X is constant.

The preceding isomorphism is exactly the unit at M of constantSheafAdj with the final etale object X -> X. Thus every component of the unit is an isomorphism, hence so is the unit natural transformation. Apply the general adjunction fact fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit. This is the already-proved definition fullyFaithfulModuleConstantSheaf in the source library; no new Lean assertion or proof hole is introduced.
